core_obligations: Reduce to affine pieces (proof lines 3100-3105): choose an affine open covering T = the union of the U_i and write U_i = Spec(A_i); for each i choose a faithfully flat ind-etale map A_i -> D_i with D_i w-contractible, so that the family of morphisms Spec(D_i) -> T is a pro-etale covering.

Check that the pieces are objects of the site (proof lines 3105-3122): it suffices to show that the cardinality of D_i is bounded by the size function applied to the size of T, since then Spec(D_i) is isomorphic to an object of the big pro-etale site by the construction of the site and the cardinality bound of the constructed category; the bound follows from the estimates on the size of affine schemes of finite type together with the explicit estimate for w-contractible rings.

Conclude (proof lines 3122-3125): the family is combinatorially equivalent to a covering of the big pro-etale site, and each Spec(D_i) is weakly contractible by the equivalence between w-contractibility and weak contractibility, which yields the stated covering by affine objects that are spectra of w-contractible rings.
proof_roadmap: Cover an affine open piece and replace it by the spectrum of a w-contractible ring, giving a pro-etale covering.
Verify the size bound that makes those spectra objects of the big site.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that every object of a big pro-etale site admits a covering by affine objects which are spectra of w-contractible rings, hence weakly contractible (statement lines 3086-3094). The proof (proof lines 3096-3127) covers an affine open piece, replaces it by a faithfully flat ind-etale extension with w-contractible ring, verifies through explicit cardinality estimates that the resulting affine schemes are objects of the big site, and concludes by the equivalence between w-contractibility and weak contractibility. H2: a construction with a genuine size estimate and three inputs, written out in full.
